title: Microsoft Copilot Chat: side pane in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote for commercial Microsoft 365 users
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a separate Copilot Chat side-pane policy, so the briefing wrongly tells administrators that disabling broader connected experiences is the only documented route. Its universal availability and default claims also go beyond the evidence, and its group-access advice omits that existing admin deployments remain honoured.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and api; Why it matters; Governance controls: first bullet; Open questions: second bullet
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate administrator setting for Copilot Chat in the Microsoft 365 app side pane.
claims.quote: Shows or hides Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat entry points in Microsoft 365 apps for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting. This policy doesn't apply to licensed users.
claims.fix: Remove controls[3] and the claim that there is no separate setting, including the corresponding open question. Replace the absence and only-broad-policy statements with: 'Microsoft documents a Copilot Chat side-pane Office Cloud Policy setting for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. The microsoft.copilot.copilotchatsidepane resource uses string value "0" to disable and "1" to enable it; it does not apply to licensed users. Tenant Configuration Management support is preview and limited to tenant-level policies, with no group-level policy configuring the target setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. Keep the broad connected-experiences control described as an existing alternative, not the only documented route.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot Chat in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote reaches the whole eligible licensed workforce, rather than depending on its Basic tier and tenant configuration.
claims.quote: Chat experiences in Microsoft 365 apps vary depending on your tenant configuration and license. ... You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.
claims.fix: Replace 'the whole licensed workforce' with 'users entitled to an in-app Copilot experience, including some users without the Copilot add-on'. Replace the summary's opening sentence with 'The launched roadmap item describes Copilot Chat side panes for commercial Microsoft 365 users; current Learn documentation says in-app access depends on licence and tenant configuration.' Replace the impact rationale's universal-access sentence with 'High. The roadmap describes access beyond Copilot add-on licence holders, while current Learn documentation distinguishes Basic users with and without in-app access.' Keep the documented tier caveat alongside the roadmap description wherever availability is stated.
